tasks.originalEssay:
The bar chart illustrates the spending patterns on consumer goods in France and the UK in 2010, expressed in pounds sterling. 

Overall, it is evident that the UK had a higher expenditure across all categories compared to France. The most significant difference was observed in the category of leisure goods, where UK consumers spent approximately £170, while their French counterparts spent around £90. 

In terms of food and drink, the UK expenditure was about £150, surpassing France's spending of approximately £110. Similarly, the UK also led in the category of clothing and footwear, with an expenditure of roughly £100, compared to France's £70. 

Notably, the least amount was spent on tobacco, where the UK recorded about £50 and France slightly less at £40. These figures indicate a clear trend of higher consumer spending in the UK across various categories, highlighting differences in consumer behavior between the two countries.

tasks.originalEssay:
Some people consider that children should be taught by their parents about how to function as productive members of society, while others regard sending children to educational institutions as the best way for them to learn this. Although the latter opinion can be advantageous in some cases, I deem that family upbringing plays a more pivotal role in educating children to be valuable members of the community.

Schools can be considered suitable places for children to learn to be good citizens. With standardized educational methods, schools can foster children’s cognitive development so that they are able to contribute to society in the future. For example, Trung Vuong school and Vinschool are well known for having nurtured successful alumni such as Professor Ngo Bao Chau and Professor Nguyen Hung, who have devoted their talents to the development of the country. However, these people only represent a small fraction of the total number of students attending schools, and thus sending children to schools cannot be the best method of educating them to be good members of society.

I perceive that parents play a more crucial role in teaching them how to be good citizens. In Vietnam, the average class size is 20 students, which makes it difficult for educators to provide proper schooling for each student. One-to-one lessons at home, on the other hand, allow children to progress faster. Furthermore, parents form stronger bonds with their offspring, and thus, it is easier for them to shape children’s personalities at an early age. For example, by telling stories such as Robin Hood and Cinderella before bedtime, parents can instill a sense of compassion and integrity in their children. These children are likely to become good members of society when they grow up.

In conclusion, although sending children to schools can be seen as a way of teaching them how to be good citizens, I believe that domestic upbringing has a more significant impact on determining who they are in the future.
